answer.policy_title: CIGNA MEDICAL COVERAGE POLICIES - MUSCULOSKELETAL CMM-312: Knee Surgery-Arthroscopic and Open Procedures
criteria_quotes: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction (with allograft or autograft) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:
• MRI, CT arthrogram, or arthroscopy shows a tear/disruption or significant laxity of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)
• Physical exam demonstrates ANY of the following findings: ◦ positive Lachman's Test ◦ positive Anterior Drawer Test ◦ positive Pivot Shift Test

• Symptoms include BOTH of the following: ◦ function-limiting knee pain and/or loss of knee function which interferes with ANY of the following: ▪ ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living ▪ demands of employment ▪ need to return to activities that require cutting, pivoting, and/or agility in which ACL insufficiency may predispose to further instability episodes that may result in new articular or meniscal cartilage injuries ◦ reports of knee instability which is noted as giving way, subjective weakness, or buckling

• Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration ◦ Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required if there is an acute injury setting and joint instability has been documented with ANY of the following additional conditions: ▪ need to return to activities that require cutting, pivoting, and/or agility in which ACL insufficiency may predispose to further instability episodes that may result in new articular or meniscal cartilage injuries
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) repair is considered not medically necessary.

Alternatively, check the denial letter or call Cigna Customer Service (1-800-882-4462 or the toll-free number on the back of the member ID card) to obtain the plan-specific fax number for commercial appeals.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The governing criteria were obtained from Cigna's public EviCore musculoskeletal guidelines. If the patient's specific benefit plan differs from standard guidelines, they can obtain the precise criteria applied by calling Cigna Customer Service at the phone number on their member ID card or requesting them in writing as part of their denial review.
answer.notes: The denial states that the documentation was incomplete. To address the medical-necessity criteria, the provider's office should submit clinical documentation containing: (1) An MRI report confirming the ACL tear/disruption; (2) Physical exam findings specifically noting a positive Lachman's, Anterior Drawer, or Pivot Shift test; (3) Clinic notes documenting knee instability (e.g., buckling, giving way) and how function-limiting pain/loss of function interferes with daily living or employment; and (4) Documentation of either 3 months of non-surgical management or explicit detail explaining that this is an acute injury setting where immediate surgical reconstruction is needed to prevent further joint injury during cutting/pivoting activities. Note that ACL repair is not covered; the surgery must be documented as an ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888).
